name: Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson Black Hole
description: Kerr's rotating black hole in a magnetic field that points along its axis of rotation and is uniform far away, the exact solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations that Jiří Podolský and Hryhorii Ovcharenko found in 2025. It is of Petrov type D, it is Kerr's metric with the field switched off and Bertotti and Robinson's universe with the mass taken away, and the spinning hole carries an electric charge.
convention: The mass parameter $m$ and the spin parameter $a$ are lengths, and the field strength $B$ is an inverse length. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Around a black hole in Melvin's magnetic universe, geodesics "cannot escape to infinity" [podolsky2025]. Frederick Ernst put Schwarzschild's hole inside that universe in 1976 and, with Walter Wild, Kerr's, using B. Kent Harrison's transformation of one solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations into another [ernst1976b, ernst1976c, harrison1968]. Their holes have been widely used to study black holes in magnetic fields [podolsky2025]. The model has its troubles: Melvin's field weakens far from the hole, the orbits of test particles can be chaotic, the ergoregion of the spinning hole runs out to infinity, and the curvature is of Petrov's type I, the most general kind [podolsky2025, gibbons2013].¶General relativity has a second universe filled by a uniform field [bertotti1959, robinson1959]. It is Tullio Levi-Civita's, from 1917, found again by Bruno Bertotti and Ivor Robinson in 1959: an anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a sphere of fixed radius, with the same field at every event [levicivita1917, bertotti1959, robinson1959]. Can a black hole stand in that field? An answer came in 1996 from George Alekseev and Alberto Garcia, a Schwarzschild black hole "immersed in a homogeneous electromagnetic field", built by a generating method of Alekseev's that "did not attract much attention because it is rather complicated" [alekseev1996, ovcharenko2026]. A second came from another direction in 2020, when Norbert Van den Bergh and John Carminati solved the Einstein-Maxwell equations for a class of fields of Petrov type D and found a family of five parameters "having the C-metric as a possible vacuum limit" [vandenbergh2020].¶The curvature of Kerr's black hole singles out two directions for light at every event, and a spacetime whose curvature does so is of type D [podolsky2025]. An electromagnetic field singles out two directions of its own, and in Kerr and Newman's charged hole, as in the whole family of Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański, the two pairs coincide [podolsky2025, plebanski1976]. In Van den Bergh and Carminati's fields they differ, and Jiří Podolský and Hryhorii Ovcharenko, at Charles University in Prague, took those fields as their starting point [vandenbergh2020, ovcharenko2026]. On 7 July 2025 they posted a spinning hole with three parameters, the mass $m$, the spin $a$, and the field strength $B$ [podolsky2025]. At $B = 0$ it is Kerr's metric, at $m = 0$ it is Bertotti and Robinson's universe, and at $a = 0$ it is a static hole that lies inside Van den Bergh and Carminati's family [podolsky2025]. They called the family the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black holes [podolsky2025].¶With no spin the horizon is at $r_h = 2m/(1 - B^2m^2)$, outside Schwarzschild's $2m$, and the innermost stable circular orbit is at $3r_h$ [podolsky2025]. The field lowers the entropy of the hole and raises its temperature [podolsky2025]. Its lines bend away from the horizon and the field is weakest in the equatorial plane, a partial version of the expulsion called the Meissner effect of black holes [podolsky2025]. The spinning hole has two horizons and a ring singularity, as Kerr's does, and its ergoregion stays near the hole [podolsky2025]. Far away the field is finite and uniform, and test particles can escape to infinity [podolsky2025].¶By 30 July 2025 Xinyu Wang, Yehui Hou, Xi Wan, Minyong Guo, and Bin Chen had computed the hole's shadow [wang2026]. The equations of a light ray split into one in $r$ and one in $\theta$, they found, and those of a massive particle in general do not [wang2026]. Finnian Gray, David Kubizňák, Ovcharenko, and Podolský traced that splitting to a hidden symmetry shared by the whole class [gray2026]. Marco Astorino put the static hole through Harrison's transformation in August 2025 and obtained a hole in both uniform fields at once, of type I [astorino2025]. Melvin's field and Bertotti and Robinson's, he wrote, "basically represent the same electromagnetic potential, but immersed in geometries with different symmetries: cylindrical the first, while spherical the latter" [astorino2025]. Alekseev and Garcia's hole of 1996 is of type D as well, and whether it is Podolský and Ovcharenko's static hole in other coordinates is not yet proved [ovcharenko2026].¶Does the hole carry a charge? Robert Wald had shown in 1974 that a spinning hole in a weak magnetic field collects the charge $2amB$, and Kerr's hole comes out of Harrison's transformation carrying it [wald1974, ernst1976c, gibbons2013]. In August 2026 Ovcharenko and Podolský integrated the electric flux through the horizon of their own hole and found a charge there too, close to $maB$ when $aB$ is small and gone when either the spin or the field is [ovcharenko2026b]. The hole with no charge is another member of a larger family, which also holds Kerr and Newman's hole, and in a weak field it is Wald's solution [ovcharenko2026b]. The static hole has no charge, and no static charged hole of type D stands in Bertotti and Robinson's magnetic field [ovcharenko2026b, ovcharenko2026].

related.text: Switch the field off, $B = 0$, and Podolský and Ovcharenko's metric is Kerr's in Boyer and Lindquist's coordinates, with $m = GM/c^2$ [podolsky2025].
With the mass taken away, $m = 0$, the metric is Bertotti and Robinson's uniform field, with spheres of radius $1/(B\sqrt{1 - B^2a^2})$ [podolsky2025].
With no spin and no field, $a = 0$ and $B = 0$, it is Schwarzschild's black hole with $r_s = 2m$.

Kerr and Newman's charged hole belongs with this one to a larger family of type D, which is Kerr and Newman's metric at $B = 0$ and holds this hole at one special value of its charge [ovcharenko2026b].

The other universe made of a uniform magnetic field. Marco Astorino found that Melvin's field and Bertotti and Robinson's carry the same potential, one in a geometry with cylindrical symmetry and the other in one with spherical symmetry [astorino2025].
The accelerating black hole. Set in Bertotti and Robinson's field it joins one family of type D with the static member of this hole, which is the one that does not accelerate [ovcharenko2026].

Kerr's hole in Melvin's magnetic universe, built by Frederick Ernst and Walter Wild in 1976. Its curvature is of Petrov type I, and its ergoregion runs out to infinity beside the axis [podolsky2025, gibbons2013].

coordinates.name: Podolský-Ovcharenko (Boyer-Lindquist)

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length; at $B = 0$ it is Kerr's $GM/c^2$ with $M$ the mass of the hole

Spin parameter, a length, with $aB < 1$; a horizon exists only for $a^2I_1^2 \le m^2I_2$, and at $a = 0$ the metric is the static hole's. The electric flux through any sphere round the hole is that of the charge $q = c^2C\,maB\sqrt{I_2}/(\sqrt{G}\,I_1)$, in Gaussian units

Strength of the field, an inverse length, $B = \sqrt{G}\,B_0/c^2$ with $B_0$ the field in Gaussian units; at $B = 0$ the metric is Kerr's, and at $m = 0$ it is Bertotti and Robinson's universe with spheres of radius $1/(B\sqrt{I_2})$. The vector potential is twice the real part of the one-form $\dfrac{c^2}{\sqrt{G}}\,\dfrac{1}{2B}\left(\partial_r\Omega\,\dfrac{a\,c\,dt - \left(r^2 + a^2\right)C\,d\phi}{r + ia\cos\theta} + \dfrac{i\,\partial_\theta\Omega}{\sin\theta}\,\dfrac{c\,dt - aC\sin^2\theta\,d\phi}{r + ia\cos\theta} + \left(\Omega - 1\right)C\,d\phi\right)$
The first of Podolský and Ovcharenko's two constants, a pure number, 1 where the spin or the field vanishes
The second of their constants, a pure number, positive for $aB < 1$
The conicity, $C = \dfrac{I_1^2}{I_1^2 + B^2\left(m^2I_2 - a^2I_1^2\right)}$, which is $1/P$ on the axis; with it both halves of the axis are regular for $\phi$ of period $2\pi$
The quadratic whose roots are the horizons $r_\pm$; at $B = 0$ it is Kerr's $r^2 - 2mr + a^2$
Kerr's $\Sigma$, which vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\theta = \pi/2$
The function of the polar angle in Podolský and Ovcharenko's line element, 1 on the equator and $1/C$ on the axis
The function of the radius in their line element, which vanishes on the horizons

The conformal factor of their line element, $ds^2 = \Omega^{-2}\left(-\dfrac{Q}{\Sigma}\left(c\,dt - aC\sin^2\theta\,d\phi\right)^2 + \dfrac{\Sigma}{Q}dr^2 + \dfrac{\Sigma}{P}d\theta^2 + \dfrac{P\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\left(a\,c\,dt - \left(r^2 + a^2\right)C\,d\phi\right)^2\right)$; on a horizon $\Omega^2 = 1 + B^2r^2$ at every $\theta$
The combination Podolský and Ovcharenko write $R$; the circle of $\phi$ has the squared radius $C^2A\sin^2\theta/(\Sigma\Omega^2)$
Dragging rate, an inverse length: an observer with no angular momentum circles at $d\phi/dt = c\,\omega/C$; on a horizon it is $a/(r^2 + a^2)$ at every $\theta$
The squared lapse of the slices of constant $t$
The factor on the plane of $r$ and $\theta$
The squared radius of the circle of $\phi$ over $C^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Podolský and Ovcharenko's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, which are Boyer and Lindquist's at $B = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ their angle divided by $C$, and write their line element in the functions $N$, $F$, $W$, and $\omega$ that the parameters define. The horizons are at the roots $r_\pm$ of $\Delta$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, with $Bm < 1$; at $B = 0$ it is Schwarzschild's $GM/c^2$ with $M$ the mass of the hole

Strength of the field, an inverse length, $B = \sqrt{G}\,B_0/c^2$ with $B_0$ the field in Gaussian units; at $B = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's, and at $m = 0$ it is Bertotti and Robinson's universe with spheres of radius $1/B$. The vector potential is the one-form $\dfrac{c^2}{\sqrt{G}}\,\dfrac{C}{B}\left(\Omega - 1 - r\,\partial_r\Omega\right)d\phi$
The conicity, $C = \dfrac{1}{1 + B^2m^2}$, which is $1/P$ on the axis; with it both halves of the axis are regular for $\phi$ of period $2\pi$
The function of the polar angle in Podolský and Ovcharenko's line element, 1 on the equator and $1/C$ on the axis
The function of the radius in their line element, which vanishes on the horizon $r_h$, where the surface gravity is $c^2\left(1 + B^2m^2\right)^2/(4m)$
The conformal factor; it is $\sqrt{1 + B^2r^2}$ on the equator and on the horizon, and $1 + B^2mr$ on the axis

coordinates.convention: We use Podolský and Ovcharenko's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ for the hole with no spin, $a = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ their angle divided by $C$. The horizon is at $r_h = 2m/(1 - B^2m^2)$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
